author: reek
body: These evaluate by de Casteljau's construction, repeated linear interpolation, rather than by summing basis weights. The reason is exactness at the cases a curve is defined by, and it took two attempts to get there.

author: reek
body: A lerp has no such problem. Interpolating between two EQUAL points answers that point for any t, because the difference is zero before it is scaled, so a curve whose control points coincide is exact by construction rather than by arithmetic luck. Endpoints and evenly spaced collinear points are exact for the same reason.
